steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 1/19

narration.label: p1-b1-c1.mp3
narration.transcript: After an image is flattened, how does a network know which pixels are neighbors?

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 1/19 · After an image is flattened, how does a network know which pixels are neighbors?

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 2/19

narration.label: p1-b1-c2.mp3
narration.transcript: At the upper left is a four-by-four image with cells numbered zero through fifteen.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 2/19 · At the upper left is a four-by-four image with cells numbered zero through fifteen.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 3/19

narration.label: p1-b1-c3.mp3
narration.transcript: The orange cell is number five.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 3/19 · The orange cell is number five.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 4/19

narration.label: p1-b1-c4.mp3
narration.transcript: The blue cells are its neighbors above, below, left, and right.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 4/19 · The blue cells are its neighbors above, below, left, and right.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 5/19

narration.label: p1-b2-c1.mp3
narration.transcript: The strip below lays the rows of the image end to end.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 5/19 · The strip below lays the rows of the image end to end.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 6/19

narration.label: p1-b2-c2.mp3
narration.transcript: Row p, column q becomes position four p plus q in the strip.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 6/19 · Row p, column q becomes position four p plus q in the strip.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 7/19

narration.label: p1-b2-c3.mp3
narration.transcript: Cells four and six still sit on either side of cell five.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 7/19 · Cells four and six still sit on either side of cell five.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 8/19

narration.label: p1-b2-c4.mp3
narration.transcript: Its upper neighbor, cell one, is now four positions to the left.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 8/19 · Its upper neighbor, cell one, is now four positions to the left.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 9/19

narration.label: p1-b2-c5.mp3
narration.transcript: Its lower neighbor, cell nine, is four positions to the right.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 9/19 · Its lower neighbor, cell nine, is four positions to the right.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 10/19

narration.label: p1-b2-c6.mp3
narration.transcript: Each row has four cells, so moving vertically by one pixel means jumping a whole row in the strip.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 10/19 · Each row has four cells, so moving vertically by one pixel means jumping a whole row in the strip.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 11/19

narration.label: p1-b3-c1.mp3
narration.transcript: Flattening also creates apparent neighbors.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 11/19 · Flattening also creates apparent neighbors.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 12/19

narration.label: p1-b3-c2.mp3
narration.transcript: Cell three, outlined in red, is at the far right of the top row.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 12/19 · Cell three, outlined in red, is at the far right of the top row.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 13/19

narration.label: p1-b3-c3.mp3
narration.transcript: Cell four is at the far left of the next row, well away from cell three.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 13/19 · Cell four is at the far left of the next row, well away from cell three.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 14/19

narration.label: p1-b3-c4.mp3
narration.transcript: Yet the red bracket shows that three and four touch in the strip.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 14/19 · Yet the red bracket shows that three and four touch in the strip.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 15/19

narration.label: p1-b4-c1.mp3
narration.transcript: Flattening preserves every pixel value.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 15/19 · Flattening preserves every pixel value.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 16/19

narration.label: p1-b4-c2.mp3
narration.transcript: The issue is how a fully connected layer treats positions.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 16/19 · The issue is how a fully connected layer treats positions.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 17/19

narration.label: p1-b4-c3.mp3
narration.transcript: Shuffle the inputs and their corresponding weights together, and the result stays the same.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 17/19 · Shuffle the inputs and their corresponding weights together, and the result stays the same.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 18/19

narration.label: p1-b4-c4.mp3
narration.transcript: The layer has no built-in sense of which pixels are neighbors.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 18/19 · The layer has no built-in sense of which pixels are neighbors.

steps.label: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 19/19

narration.label: p1-b4-c5.mp3
narration.transcript: It needs examples to learn local patterns such as edges.

steps.speakerNotes: Flattening hides the neighborhood structure · 19/19 · It needs examples to learn local patterns such as edges.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 1/33

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 5/33

narration.transcript: On the right, the feature map stores the result at each kernel position.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 5/33 · On the right, the feature map stores the result at each kernel position.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 6/33

narration.transcript: The equation on the right defines the sliding calculation.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 6/33 · The equation on the right defines the sliding calculation.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 7/33

narration.label: p2-b2-c2.mp3
narration.transcript: S at i, j is the output in row i, column j of the feature map.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 7/33 · S at i, j is the output in row i, column j of the feature map.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 8/33

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 8/33 · The indices m and n run over the cells of the kernel.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 9/33 · The corresponding pixel is in image row i plus m, column j plus n.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 10/33

narration.label: p2-b2-c5.mp3
narration.transcript: Overlay the kernel, multiply matching cells, and add the products.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 10/33 · Overlay the kernel, multiply matching cells, and add the products.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 11/33

narration.label: p2-b3-c1.mp3
narration.transcript: Try the orange window in the upper left.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 11/33 · Try the orange window in the upper left.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 12/33

narration.label: p2-b3-c2.mp3
narration.transcript: Only the ones in the kernel contribute.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 12/33 · Only the ones in the kernel contribute.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 13/33

narration.label: p2-b3-c3.mp3
narration.transcript: All five of them land on ones in the image.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 13/33 · All five of them land on ones in the image.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 14/33

narration.label: p2-b3-c4.mp3
narration.transcript: Their row and column coordinates are zero zero, zero two, one one, two zero, and two two.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 14/33 · Their row and column coordinates are zero zero, zero two, one one, two zero, and two two.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 15/33

narration.transcript: So the top-left output is five ones added together, or five.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 15/33 · So the top-left output is five ones added together, or five.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 16/33

narration.label: p2-b3-c6.mp3
narration.transcript: The window matches the kernel exactly, giving the largest possible response here.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 16/33 · The window matches the kernel exactly, giving the largest possible response here.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 17/33

narration.transcript: Now move one cell right to the purple window.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 17/33 · Now move one cell right to the purple window.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 18/33

narration.transcript: Every one in the kernel lands on a zero in the image.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 18/33 · Every one in the kernel lands on a zero in the image.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 19/33

narration.label: p2-b4-c3.mp3
narration.transcript: Each of those products is one times zero.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 19/33 · Each of those products is one times zero.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 20/33

narration.transcript: So the output at row zero, column one is zero.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 20/33 · So the output at row zero, column one is zero.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 21/33

narration.label: p2-b4-c5.mp3
narration.transcript: The two patterns are completely out of alignment.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 21/33 · The two patterns are completely out of alignment.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 22/33

narration.label: p2-b4-c6.mp3
narration.transcript: The kernel is unchanged. The response changes with the pattern under it.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 22/33 · The kernel is unchanged. The response changes with the pattern under it.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 23/33

narration.transcript: Continue across the image, moving down one row at a time.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 23/33 · Continue across the image, moving down one row at a time.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 24/33

narration.label: p2-b5-c2.mp3

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 24/33 · Only positions where the whole kernel fits are allowed.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 25/33

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 25/33 · In each direction there are five minus three plus one, or three positions.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 26/33

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 26/33 · The kernel takes up three cells, leaving fewer places where it can start.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 27/33

narration.transcript: The feature map is therefore three by three.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 27/33 · The feature map is therefore three by three.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 28/33

narration.label: p2-b5-c6.mp3
narration.transcript: Its first row is five, zero, five.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 28/33 · Its first row is five, zero, five.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 29/33

narration.label: p2-b5-c7.mp3
narration.transcript: Its second row is zero, five, zero.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 29/33 · Its second row is zero, five, zero.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 30/33

narration.label: p2-b5-c8.mp3
narration.transcript: Its third row is five, zero, five again.

steps.speakerNotes: Slide a small kernel over the image · 30/33 · Its third row is five, zero, five again.

steps.label: Slide a small kernel over the image · 31/33

narration.label: p2-b6-c1.mp3
narration.transcript: The green cells mark matches, making a smaller checkerboard.

steps.label: Two constraints cut 256 weights to 9 · 1/35

steps.speakerNotes: Two constraints cut 256 weights to 9 · 1/35 · Let's keep the task fixed, with a four-by-four input and a four-by-four output.

steps.speakerNotes: Two constraints cut 256 weights to 9 · 2/35 · How many weights does each wiring scheme need?

steps.speakerNotes: Two constraints cut 256 weights to 9 · 3/35 · Compare full connectivity, local connections, and local connections with a shared kernel.
